title: Chaos and the Julia set of the complex exponential
abstract: Formalizes the dynamics of z ↦ exp(z): escaping points, points with dense forward orbit, and repelling periodic points are dense in the complex plane; the map is chaotic in Devaney's sense and its Julia set is the whole plane. The development proves eventual covering of every compact set omitting zero, constructs contracting inverse branches, and rules out every locally uniform spherical subsequential limit on nonempty open sets. It includes general normal-sequence restriction lemmas, quantitative open mapping, and a two-target obstruction for arbitrary separated uniform codomains. The Lean proofs were primarily generated by AI under Lasse Rempe's direction. The initial six-lemma architecture adapts John Harrison's HOL Light formalization, credited with its retained BSD notice in the entry module.

informal.ExpChaotic.devaney_chaotic: The complex exponential is continuous, has dense periodic points, and the monoid action generated by its iterates is topologically transitive on the complex plane.
informal.ExpChaotic.juliaSet_exp: The Julia set of the complex exponential is the whole plane, where the Fatou set is defined by local normality of sphere-valued iterates with arbitrary locally uniform sphere-valued limits.
informal.ExpChaotic.dense_repellingPeriodicSet: Points p with a positive period n and derivative norm greater than one for the nth exponential iterate are dense in the complex plane.
informal.ExpChaotic.eventually_covers_compact: For every nonempty open set U in the complex plane and every compact set K omitting zero, all sufficiently large iterates of the exponential map send U onto a set containing K.
informal.ExpChaotic.dense_escapingSet: Points whose forward exponential orbit eventually leaves every centered Euclidean ball are dense in the complex plane.
informal.ExpChaotic.not_countable_denseOrbitSet: The set of complex points with dense forward exponential orbit is uncountable.
informal.ExpChaotic.not_tendstoLocallyUniformly_s: On every nonempty open set in the complex plane, no strictly increasing subsequence of exponential iterates converges locally uniformly to any function into the Riemann sphere.
